content: 1. Before utilizing this tool, it is essential to identify the stakeholders who will require the information. This can be achieved by using the Stakeholder Mapping Guide Tool. 2. Understand the importance of disseminating the guidelines and the mechanisms by which dissemination operates. 3. Clearly define the expectations of dissemination for specific stakeholders by analyzing the desired outcomes. 4. Establish indicators to measure the success of dissemination efforts. Record your target measurements in the designated sections on the third page of this tool. Dissemination refers to the intentional distribution of information and materials to a specific clinical practice audience. The primary goal is to promote the adoption of standardized country family planning guidelines. Dissemination can occur at three levels: policy, practice, and provider. For dissemination to be effective, each level must address three critical components: who, what, and how. The who refers to the stakeholders, which include individuals or organizations that benefit from the dissemination. The what refers to the outcomes, which are the reasons for conducting dissemination. The how refers to the indicators, which are the methods used to measure the success of dissemination. At each level, the implementation team must determine the most effective way to gather feedback on the indicators. A dissemination model is provided to outline, at each level (policy, practice, and provider), who the stakeholders are, what the outcomes are, and how the outcomes will be measured. Stakeholders (Who): Policymakers Professional and health service delivery organizations, academia, and other partners Providers Outcomes (What): Providing feedback on the content and usability of guidelines and tools Contributing to the practice-policy feedback loop Facilitating peer-to-peer dissemination Enhancing readiness for implementation Increasing the use of guidelines Expanding knowledge and awareness Supporting readiness for implementation Contributing to the practice-policy feedback loop Providing information or impetus for policy change Influencing policy impact Participating in timely updates of guidelines Advocating for guideline adoption Increasing knowledge and awareness Indicators (How): Number of organizations sharing the guidance Number of conferences where information is presented Number of organizations adopting, adapting, or endorsing the guidelines Number of organizations developing tools based on the guidelines Number of organizations with representatives promoting guideline use Number of organizations providing feedback on the guidelines Number of policy changes made by organizations in response to the guidance Number of relevant policies assessed Percentage of updated recommendations from MEC/SPR incorporated into the guidance Mechanisms in place for policymakers to receive experiential feedback from providers Percentage of relevant policymaking entities demonstrating financial and other support for the guidelines Number of policymakers with shared language and values relevant to the guidelines Mechanisms in place for providers to receive experiential feedback from policymakers Number of providers aware of the guidelines Number of providers serving in facilities receiving the guidelines Number of providers receiving training on the guidelines Number of providers knowledgeable about updates to the guidelines Increased knowledge scores among providers Evidence-based, standardized, high-quality practices implemented Number of providers reporting the use of the guidelines Number of providers advocating for the use of evidence-based guidelines and practices Number of providers receiving training Increase in the number of providers receiving training or seeking guidance Number of organizations participating in timely updates of the guidelines The implementation team should determine the indicators by which successful dissemination will be measured and document the target measurements in the appropriate sections.
